title: How Honored Is the Place
description: How Honored Is the Place in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 654 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Safety of the Church”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How hon-ored is the place Where we a-dor-ing stand! Zi-on, the glo-ry of the earth, And beau-ty of the land.

lines: Zion, the glory of the earth,
While walls, of strong salvation made,
You that have known Jehovah's name,
Trust in the Lord, ye saints,
Strength in the Lord Jehovah dwells,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
